segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: Products & Systems Integration vs Software & Services
segmentRevenue.content:
Motorola Solutions reports two segments. Products and Systems Integration (P&SI) is the land-mobile-radio hardware, infrastructure and video/command-center systems business. Software and Services is the recurring, higher-margin layer: managed/support services, cloud software (CommandCentral, Cloud video storage) and the ASTRO 25 network-as-a-service contracts.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: Software & Services was roughly 38% of FY2025 revenue and growing faster than P&SI as more of the install base shifts to subscriptions -- the segment mix, not blended Revenue, is where the re-rating thesis sits.

What to watch:

  • Software & Services growing as a share of total revenue
  • P&SI growth concentrated in large multi-year radio contract wins (lumpy by quarter)

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income: P&SI vs Software & Services
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income split the same way as segment revenue -- it is not derivable by applying the group operating margin to each segment's revenue, since the two carry different cost structures.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: Software & Services' margin should expand faster than P&SI's as the subscription base scales; a segment-margin chart catches that before it shows up in the blended OperatingMargin line above.

What to watch:

  • Software & Services margin expanding ahead of P&SI's
  • Either segment's margin compressing while the other masks it in the group total

productLineRevenue.title: Revenue by product line: MCN, Video, Command Center
productLineRevenue.content:
Three disclosed product lines sit inside the two segments. MCN (Mission-Critical Communications/Networks, formerly branded LMR) is the core radio and network business and by far the largest. Video is fixed and body-worn video/surveillance (Avigilon, VideoManager). Command Center is the 911/dispatch software (CommandCentral Aware, computer-aided dispatch).

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: Video and Command Center are the smaller, faster-growing lines management highlights on every call as the diversification away from radio hardware -- MCN's growth rate alone understates the group story.

What to watch:

  • Video and Command Center growing faster than MCN
  • MCN deceleration offset (or not) by the other two lines

backlog.title: Backlog by segment
backlog.content:
Backlog is contracted, unrecognized future revenue -- Motorola's main forward-visibility metric, reported for the group and split between the two segments.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: Software & Services backlog (multi-year ASTRO 25/cloud contracts) has grown to roughly three-quarters of the total even though it is the smaller segment by revenue, which is the clearest single number for the subscription-mix thesis. P&SI backlog has been flat to declining over the same years. FY-only: backlog is disclosed at fiscal year-end, not each quarter.

What to watch:

  • Software & Services backlog continuing to outgrow P&SI's
  • Total backlog growth versus trailing revenue growth (book-to-bill)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Motorola Solutions, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
